newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada makes $720 million bid for Britain's Clyde.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada makes $720 million bid for Britain's Clyde.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources on Wednesday launched a 432 million British pound ($720 million) hostile bid for the British oil firm, Clyde Petroleum, but analysts believe the Calgary, Alberta-based company will have to offer more to secure a deal.
Analysts said the rise in Clyde's shares, which surged 33 pence (54 cents) to close at 118 pence ($1.93), well above Gulf Canada's cash offer of 105 pence a share ($1.72).
"The share price is telling you -- and I tend to agree -- that this bid is not going to be enough," said Nick Antill, an analyst at the brokerage house BZW.
Clyde rejected the offer, saying it was "unsolicited and wholly unacceptable."
"This offer is far too low and anyway Clyde will continue to deliver better value to shareholders as an independent company," Clyde's Chairman Malcolm Gourlay told Reuters.
Gulf Canada's bid comes hot on the heels of the $1.23 billion acquisition earlier this month of London-based Santa Fe Exploration by Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA.

"The offer for Clyde follows Gulf Canada's previously stated desire to increase its activities outside its existing core areas of North America and Indonesia," J. P. Bryan, chief executive of Gulf Canada said.
Clyde's North Sea and Australian assets would provide Gulf Canada with additional core areas, and Clyde's Indonesian assets would complement its existing assets, the Canadian firm said.
The company this year considered a bid for Australia's Command Petroleum Holdings NL, which instead became the takeover target of Britain's Cairn Energy Plc.
